key_insight: FLORE aims to teach humanoids to coordinate contact forces with hand and whole-body motion, rather than relying on movement trajectories alone. It captures demonstrations without requiring a robot during data collection.
problem_solved: Everyday physical tasks require coordinated force control across both hands and the body—information that motion-only demonstrations cannot fully capture.
method: Record hand motion and contact forces and torques using two force-sensing UMI-style handheld grippers.
Capture body motion simultaneously with wearable trackers.
Use these demonstrations within FLORE to learn force-reactive humanoid loco-manipulation; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not describe the remaining learning pipeline.
impact: Combining force measurements with motion demonstrations could support humanoid learning for contact-rich tasks. Robot-free data collection offers a practical route to gathering demonstrations, although the provided excerpt reports no evaluation results.
visual_elements: Demonstration setup showing two instrumented handheld grippers and wearable body trackers.
Humanoid silhouette with arrows illustrating coordinated hand forces and whole-body motion.
Side-by-side comparison of motion-only trajectories and trajectories enriched with force and torque signals.
Pipeline diagram: robot-free demonstrations → motion and contact data → force-reactive humanoid behavior.
